title: Coq au Vin
subtitle: French braised chicken with pancetta, mushrooms, and red wine
excerpt: A slow-braised French chicken dish with pancetta, mushrooms, and red wine. The sauce reduces to something rich and glossy, and the dish only gets better the next day.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from the classic French braise. Red wine vinegar replaces wine for a sharper, quicker sauce that still gives the characteristic depth.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool fully and freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge and reheat gently on the hob.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead and reheat. The flavour deepens overnight.

content.text: Brown the chicken well before adding any liquid. That colour is where most of the flavour in the final dish comes from.
Pat the chicken dry and season well. Heat half the butter in a large stockpot over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken in batches, skin-side down, for 4 to 5 minutes per side. Remove and set aside.
Add the pancetta to the pot and fry for 3 minutes until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining butter. Cook the onion and carrot over medium heat for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and tomato puree. Stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the red wine vinegar. Scrape the bottom of the pot to lift any stuck bits. Add the stock, thyme, and bay leaves.
Return the chicken and pancetta to the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low heat for 40 minutes.
Remove the lid. Add the mushrooms and cook uncovered for 15 more minutes until the sauce has thickened and the chicken is very tender.
Discard the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Taste and season. Scatter parsley over the top before serving.

items.cause: Lid was left on during the final stage.
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer uncovered for at least 15 minutes.

items.symptom: Chicken skin is soft, not golden.
items.cause: Too much liquid covered the skin during braising.
items.fix: Position chicken pieces skin-side up above the sauce level.

items.cause: Vinegar not reduced enough before stock was added.
items.fix: Next time reduce the vinegar by half before adding stock.
